answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can bind one staked bond to a unique cryptographic identity kernel that every agent must present before its messages count. Cloned accounts are hollow because they reuse one kernel or split a single bond, and audits trace that reuse and slash the stake. An attacker seeking many voices must lock fresh capital for each fake identity, so the cost climbs linearly with every extra vote. A quiet whisper from a paid sybil then carries no more weight than one from a genuine agent: influence must be bought with capital that can be seized.
